problems.title: A single-draw quantile does not bound a fixed maximum
problems.source_location: Introduction, PDF p.3; Section 2.1, PDF p.4, paragraph after Problem 1
claim: Section 2.1 constrains one draw from the shard but describes its threshold as a probabilistic bound on every shard value.
analysis: Use query \((1,0)\), ninety-nine points \((0,j)\), \(1\leq j\leq99\), and one point \((100,0)\). Mean score is \(1\), variance \(99\), and maximum \(100\). At \(\delta=0.8\), threshold \(1\) already covers \(0.99\) of one-draw scores, above the required \(0.9\), yet the fixed maximum is still \(100\). Even \(1+3\sqrt{99}\) is below that maximum without violating the one-draw lemma.
result: The confidence interpretation is too strong. The quantile-ranking objective remains mathematically valid.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Describe a single-point upper quantile. For a fixed shard of size \(n\), the deterministic moment bound is \(\max s_i\leq m+\sqrt{(n-1)v}\); a future maximum has a different probability law.
problems.impact_rationale: This corrects a probabilistic interpretation, without disproving the routing heuristic or measured recall.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Two-sided sketch error does not preserve one-sided coverage
problems.source_location: Section 2.3, PDF pp.5–6; Definition 1, Eq.(8), Lemma 2 and Algorithm 1
claim: The router substitutes a masked covariance sketch into the exact-covariance quantile score. Lemma 2 controls approximation error, not covariance domination.
analysis: Take orthonormal vectors \(u=(1,1,0,0)/\sqrt2\), \(q=(0,0,1,1)/\sqrt2\), \(r=(1,-1,0,0)/\sqrt2\), \(s=(0,0,1,-1)/\sqrt2\). For each group \((n,a)=(7,\sqrt{18/5})\) or \((18,-7/\sqrt{90})\), set \(\theta_j=2\pi j/n\), \(0\leq j<n\), and \[x_{n,j}=a q+\sqrt{18/5}\cos\theta_j\,u+\sqrt{2/5}\sin\theta_j\,r+\sqrt{6/5}\cos(2\theta_j)\,s.\] Finite trigonometric sums give mean zero and covariance with diagonal ones and correlation blocks \(4/5\), \(2/5\). Its eigenvalues along \(u,q,r,s\) are \(9/5,7/5,1/5,3/5\). The rank-one masked sketch is \(I+(4/5)uu^\top\), so query variance is \(1\) instead of \(7/5\). At \(\delta=1/2\), threshold \(\sqrt3\) lies below the seven positive scores \(\sqrt{18/5}\), covering only \(18/25=0.72<0.75\). Exact threshold \(\sqrt{21/5}\) covers all points. The sketch’s spectral error still satisfies Lemma 2; two-sided approximation does not imply covariance domination.
result: The exact quantile guarantee cannot be inherited automatically. No separately stated universal sketch-coverage theorem or benchmark recall is refuted.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Inflate the quadratic form by \(D_{\max}\max(\lambda_{t+1},0)\|q\|^2\), where \(\lambda_{t+1}\) is the largest discarded normalized residual eigenvalue. This upper-bounds omitted positive variance and restores the one-draw guarantee under the original lemma’s assumptions.
problems.impact_rationale: This is an approximation limitation, not an invalidity of the proved two-sided sketch lemma.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Normalized-centroid optimism requires nonnegative score
claim: The introductory argument infers an increased score merely from a centroid norm at most one.
analysis: Unit points \((-1/2,\pm\sqrt3/2)\) have centroid \((-1/2,0)\). Query \((1,0)\) gives score \(-1/2\), which becomes \(-1\) after centroid normalization. Division by a norm below one raises a nonnegative score but lowers a negative one.
result: The positive-score intuition survives with its sign condition. A zero centroid also needs a convention.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is an introductory scope correction, not central algorithm failure.
problems.existing_correction_status: No validated correction is established for this item.
